latest.content:

RNS Number : 1572W
TomCo Energy PLC
24 September 2026
24 September 2026
TOMCO ENERGY PLC
(“TomCo” or the “Company”)
Update re
:
Valkor LLC’s Asphalt Ridge Project, drilling plans
and Greenfield, Utah, USA
TomCo (AIM: TOM),
the US operating oil development group focused on using innovative technology to unlock unconventional hydrocarbon resources
, is pleased to provide an update on progress made by Valkor LLC (“Valkor”), its technical contractor and 50:50 partner in Greenfield Energy, LLC (“Greenfield”), with respect to its neighbouring Asphalt Ridge Project including installation of its planned demonstration plant and wider area drilling plans. Greenfield is expected to be afforded the opportunity to participate in one or more wells, subject to funding, with such activity deemed of strategic importance to the USA as a current net importer of heavy oil.
Valkor’s Asphalt Ridge Project
Valkor has informed the Company that a re-entry and production start programme is commencing on the original vertical pilot wells on its Asphalt Ridge acreage, incorporating the findings from a recent comprehensive study by Core Laboratories Inc. that confirmed the technical viability of Valkor’s modified enhanced oil recovery methodology to exploit the resource. Production is anticipated to be at a low rate of 20 to 40 barrels of oil per day (“bopd”). Subject to such pilot wells being successful, Valkor then expects to commence an initial eight-well horizontal drilling programme on both its own and Greenfield’s subsidiary, AC Oil, LLC’s (“AC Oil”), leased acreage targeting production of approximately 250 to 300 bopd of heavy oil per well at a cost of approximately $6m per well.
Pursuant to its existing agreement and partnership with Valkor, and subject to the Company raising the requisite funding, TomCo anticipates participating in one or more of the abovementioned wells in return for a proportionate production/revenue share based on the funding amount contributed.
Site installation works for Valkor’s 500 bopd demonstration mined oil-sands separation plant are also underway, with asphalt production expected to commence in Q1 2027.
Once commercially proven, TomCo will then have the opportunity, as previously announced, to pursue the potential financing, construction and commissioning of a similar, but much larger 5,000 bopd mined oil-sands separation plant, on tract D of AC Oil’s lease area which would be operated by Greenfield and subject to certain profit sharing and royalty arrangements between the parties.
FocusIR Interview
Steven Byle, a Non-Executive Director of the Company and the founder and Chief Executive Officer of Valkor, has recently recorded an online interview with FocusIR with respect to Valkor’s plans and drilling activities at Asphalt Ridge including an outline of expected timings and implications for TomCo should the Company be able to fund its planned participation in due course. This recording is available at
https://media.focusir.com/Valkor-TomCo
and will shortly be made available on the Company’s website at
www.tomcoenergy.com
.
Appointment of Greenfield’s CEO
Further to the Company’s announcement of 29 June 2026, the Company and Valkor have now formally agreed terms for the appointment of Mavriky Kalugin, who has directly relevant technical expertise and practical experience of operating projects of a similar nature, to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Greenfield. He is expected to commence work at Greenfield in October 2026, initially working alongside the team constructing Valkor’s pilot demonstration plant and advising on the optimisation of Valkor’s drilling programme.

TomCo Energy plc
("TomCo", the "Company" or the "Group")
Unaudited interim results for the six month period ended 31 March 2026
TomCo (AIM: TOM), the US operating oil development group focused on using innovative technology to unlock unconventional hydrocarbon resources, announces its unaudited interim results for the six month period ended 31 March 2026.
Chairman's Statement
During the period under review, the Company has continued to focus on pursuing its strategy in Utah, with a particular emphasis on strengthening its relationship with its principal contractor and technical partner, Valkor LLC ("Valkor"), in order to progress its plans for Greenfield Energy, LLC ("Greenfield"). In February 2026, the Company announced a renewed and closer partnership with Valkor,
such that Greenfield is now 50:50 jointly owned and controlled by TomCo and Valkor. The intention going forwards is to jointly seek to exploit Greenfield's existing leased oil-sands acreage and in situ resources in the Uinta Basin, Utah, USA, together with the Group's intellectual and technological expertise.
A
longside this key development
,
the Company successfully completed a
£550,000 gross
equity fundraising by way of a placing and subscription, to secure additional working capital and strengthen the Group's financial position. As part of the new arrangements with Valkor, the existing loan facility between Greenfield and Valkor was amended and restated, including the settlement of part of the outstanding balance through the issue of new ordinary shares in TomCo, and the remaining balance now scheduled for repayment in February 2027.
In addition, Steven Byle, Valkor's founder and Chief Executive Officer, joined the Company's board of directors ("Board") as a Non-Executive Director, thereby further aligning the interests of both parties and strengthening the Group's operational and technical capabilities.
Valkor continues to advance its neighbouring Asphalt Ridge project in Utah, including progressing the construction of a fully funded oil-sands separation plant (targeted to be operational by the end of this year) and the testing and refinement of drilling and heating methodologies to achieve commercial heavy oil extraction. A successful outcome from such activities is expected to support, the potential joint development of Greenfield's leased acreage in 2027. Accordingly, together with Valkor, we are in the process of appointing a Chief Executive Officer to lead Greenfield, namely Mavriky Kalugin who is originally from Alaska. Mavriky has directly relevant technical expertise and practical experience of operating projects of a similar nature to what we have planned as we seek to create and deliver long term value for our shareholders.
Pursuant to the terms of our agreement, and subject to securing the necessary funding in due course, the Group has the potential to participate in the drilling of one or more wells on Greenfield's acreage alongside Valkor and other potential investors, and, in the longer term, to pursue potential oil-sands separation activities via the construction of a plant through Greenfield. While a number of practical and financial challenges remain, our renewed partnership with Valkor provides a clearer pathway for the future development of the Group's assets, and the Board remains focussed on bringing these opportunities to fruition.

UNAUDITED NOTES FORMING PART OF THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED INTERIM FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
For the six months ended 31 March 2026
1.
Accounting Policies
Basis of Preparation
The unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements of TomCo Energy plc ("TomCo" or the "Company") for the six months ended 31 March 2026, comprise the Company and its subsidiaries (together referred to as the "Group").
The unaudited condensed interim financial information for the Group has been prepared using the recognition and measurement requirements of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS and IFRIC interpretations) issued by the International Accounting Standards Board ("IASB") as adopted for use in the EU, with the exception of IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting that is not mandatory for companies quoted on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange. The unaudited condensed interim financial information has been prepared using the accounting policies which will be applied in the Group's statutory financial information for the year ending 30 September 2026.
There were no new standards, interpretations and amendments to published standards effective in the period which had a significant impact on the Group.
Going concern
The Directors have prepared a cash flow forecast for the period to 30 June 2027 which shows that based on its currently anticipated outgoings, the Group will need to raise additional funds by November 2026 in order to continue as a going concern for the next 12 months.
Based on a history of successfully raising additional working capital when needed, the Directors currently have a reasonable expectation that the Group will be able to raise the required additional funds. These conditions represent a material uncertainty which may cast significant doubt over the Group's ability to continue as a going concern such that it may be unable to realise its assets and discharge its liabilities in the normal course of business.
Whilst acknowledging this material uncertainty, the Directors remain confident of raising additional funds such that the Directors consider it appropriate to prepare the unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial information on a going concern basis which presumes that the Group will be able to meet its obligations as they fall due for the foreseeable future. The Board's ability to raise such funds cannot be guaranteed. The unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements do not include the adjustments that would result if the Group was unable to continue as a going concern.
2. Financial reporting period
The unaudited condensed interim financial information incorporates comparative figures for the unaudited six month interim period to 31 March 2025 and the audited financial year ended 30 September 2025. The six-month financial information to 31 March 2026 is neither audited nor reviewed. The Directors consider the unaudited condensed interim financial information for the period to be a fair representation of the financial position, results from operations and cash flows for the period in conformity with the generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied.
The financial information contained in this unaudited interim report does not constitute statutory accounts as defined by the Isle of Man Companies Act 2006. It does not include all disclosures that would otherwise be required in a complete set of financial statements and should be read in conjunction with the 2025 Annual Report and Financial Statements. The comparatives for the full year ended 30 September 2025 are not the Group's full statutory accounts for that year. The auditors' report on those accounts contained an emphasis of matter regarding a material uncertainty related to going concern.

TomCo (AIM: TOM), the US operating oil development group focused on using innovative technology to unlock unconventional hydrocarbon resources, is pleased to announce, further to the Company's announcement of 23 February 2026 and completion of the Company's Nominated Adviser's customary due diligence process, that Mr Steven Byle has been appointed as a Non-Executive Director of the Company with immediate effect. In addition, the Company has granted share options ("Options") over, in aggregate 605,463,529 ordinary shares of no par value each ("Ordinary Shares") in the capital of the Company as detailed further below.

company_30s.what_they_do: Tomco Energy is a small oil‑and‑gas exploration company that focuses on developing a 5,000‑barrels‑per‑day oil field in the Greenfield area of the UK. The company’s main asset is a partnership with a U.S. developer, Valkor, which owns a 50% stake in the field and will provide the capital and technical expertise to start production.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Oil and gas exploration remains a key driver of global energy supply. Tomco’s partnership gives it access to a potentially high‑yield field that could add a steady stream of cash to the market. If the field comes on stream, it would make the company a relevant player in the UK’s renewable‑energy‑transition‑friendly energy mix, which is attractive to investors looking for lower‑carbon assets.
company_30s.current_state: Tomco is still in the early stages of development. It has announced drilling plans and secured a partnership with Valkor, but it has not yet produced any commercial volumes. The company is still raising capital and refining its business model, which keeps the stock highly speculative.

rns_narrative: Tomco is actively working with Valkor to move a 5,000‑bopd oil field from the planning stage to drilling. The latest updates focus on drilling schedules, partnership agreements, and the expected timeline for production.

The company has been rotating through a series of management and option‑grant announcements that suggest it is building a lean, focused leadership team. These moves are meant to reassure investors that the company is serious about delivering results.

There is a clear narrative that Tomco is trying to secure funding and partnership terms that will allow the field to become a viable revenue generator. The company’s recent RNs emphasize that the partnership will bring in the necessary capital, while the company will retain a controlling share of the production.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – a handful of traders see value but most are silent, waiting for a clear sign that funding is secured.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls argue that the partnership with Valkor and the upcoming drilling schedule mean the company is on the verge of turning the field into a cash‑generating asset. They see the current low price as a buying window.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company still needs a sizeable capital raise and that the partnership terms might not be enough to cover operating costs. They also point to the lack of any production data and the high risk of drilling delays.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Over the past week sentiment has shifted from cautious optimism to a more defensive stance. While some traders are excited about the partnership, others have stepped back after hearing about potential funding hurdles.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker are flat, indicating almost no public interest. This lack of noise is a green light for contrarians, as a future announcement could trigger a surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: The drilling start‑up date announced by Valkor – if it is confirmed within the next 60 days, it could signal that the partnership is moving forward.
A capital‑raising event, such as a private placement or a convertible bond issue, would demonstrate that the company can secure the funds needed for development.
A positive technical signal, like a sudden spike in trading volume that exceeds the 3‑month average by 200%, would show that new investors are stepping in.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear, dated drilling start‑up in the next two months and a volume surge that indicates fresh money entering the stock. Also monitor any regulatory approvals or drilling permits that could remove a key obstacle.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early capitulation phase – price has fallen significantly from its recent highs and there is little trading activity. If the partnership moves forward, we expect a gradual recovery that could take 6–12 months, with a sharp rebound once production milestones are announced.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company completes the partnership and starts drilling, the field could generate significant cash flows. Given the current price, a move to halfway between the last high and the current level would represent a 200% gain. Historical data on similar deep‑crash setups shows that such a bounce can deliver double‑digit returns within a year.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the company fails to raise the necessary capital or that drilling is delayed beyond the next 12 months. In that scenario the price could fall another 20–30% before the next low point, leaving investors with a net loss of 10–15% from the current level.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside of roughly 200% versus a downside of only 10–15%. The asymmetry is clear: you can lose a small amount of capital while having the chance to double your investment if the partnership and drilling succeed.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback that confirms the start‑up date, using a position size that limits exposure to 2–3% of total capital. Place a stop 5% below the entry price to protect against a false break. Target the halfway point between the current level and the last high for a first profit lock‑in.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a confirmed drilling start‑up date and a volume spike of at least 200% over the 3‑month moving average. If those conditions are met, consider a small position to test the market’s reaction before scaling up.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to secure funding within 12 months or a regulatory body rejects the drilling plans, consider exiting the position to avoid a prolonged downtrend.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Tomco’s deep price drop and partnership with Valkor create a high‑reward contrarian play – a clear funding or drilling announcement could trigger a 200% rebound, but a failure to raise capital or delay drilling could cap losses to around 10–15%.
